claims.text: Helm installs resources in a fixed order by Kubernetes kind, defined in kind_sorter.go in the Helm repository.
Helm chart authors can't declare dependencies between resources or subcharts, except through hook weights.
Pulumi derives resource ordering from the dependency graph: each resource waits for its dependencies to become ready, and independent resources deploy in parallel.
The Helm docs state: "the Kubernetes objects from the charts and all its dependencies are aggregated into a single set; then sorted by type followed by name; and then created/updated in that order."

Helm's hardcoded kind order begins with PriorityClasses and Namespaces, then Secrets and ConfigMaps, then CustomResourceDefinitions and RBAC, then Services and workloads, with unlisted kinds (including custom resources) last.
Helm uninstall runs the same kind-ordered list in reverse.
Helm sends sorted manifests to the API server in a single pass and doesn't wait for one resource to become ready before applying the next.
A Helm subchart's objects are merged into the parent chart's set and sorted by kind, so chart dependencies don't control install order.
Helm hook resources are not managed by Helm as part of the release.
HIP-0025 proposes native sequencing for resources and subcharts in Helm and is still a draft.
Passing one resource's output into another or setting the dependsOn resource option creates an edge in Pulumi's dependency graph.
The Pulumi Kubernetes provider waits for each resource to become ready before creating resources that depend on it.
Pulumi deletes follow the dependency graph in reverse.
helm.v4.Chart supports the config.kubernetes.io/depends-on annotation for ordering between objects inside the chart, and dependsOn on the chart for dependencies outside it.
Pulumi's dependency-graph ordering with parallel deployment is faster than a strict serial sequence.
Helm merges objects from a chart and its dependencies into a single set, sorts by kind, and applies in that order, so declaring a subchart dependency doesn't make it install first.
helm.v4.Chart resources appear individually in plan output, drift detection, and state.
Pulumi resolves chart values at deploy time and orders the chart install after the resources it depends on.
Using Helm charts directly from a Pulumi program is the most common adoption pattern.
Two patterns cover most production deployments of Pulumi and Helm together.
There are three common ways to adopt Pulumi alongside or in place of Helm.
Helm records each install or upgrade as a numbered release revision, and helm rollback restores a prior revision.
A failed Pulumi update leaves the stack partially updated, and you roll forward by reverting code and running pulumi up.
